447def test_sign_of_life_event_then_tool_child_then_null_preserves_the_previous_timestamp(tmp_path):
448 paths = _paths(tmp_path)
449 hb = RoundHeartbeat(paths, "g1")
450 proc_root = tmp_path / "proc"
451 config = LivenessConfig(window_seconds=60)
452 state: dict = {"child": None}
453 probe = LivenessProbe(hb, config, lambda: state["child"], proc_root=proc_root)
454
455 now = time.time()
456 spawned = _iso(now - 100)
457
458 # Tick 1: a fresh event -> "event".
459 state["child"] = ChildActivity(
460 pid=1,
461 session_id="s1",
462 cwd="/work/g1",
463 spawned_at=spawned,
464 last_event_at=_iso(now),
465 last_event_type="assistant",
466 )
467 probe.tick()
468 payload = hb.snapshot()
469 assert payload["sign_of_life_signal"] == "event"
470 assert payload["last_sign_of_life_at"] is not None
471
472 # Tick 2: a stale event but a live fake tool child under pid 1 -> "tool_child",
473 # naming the child's cmdline head. Also give pid 1 a CPU reading so the next
474 # tick has a genuine "flat" baseline to compare against, not just a missing one.
475 _write_fake_child(proc_root, 1, ppid=0, utime=1, stime=1)
476 _write_fake_child(proc_root, 2, ppid=1, cmdline=["uv", "run", "pytest", "tests/"])
477 state["child"] = ChildActivity(
478 pid=1,
479 session_id="s1",
480 cwd="/work/g1",
481 spawned_at=spawned,
482 last_event_at=_iso(now - 3600),
483 last_event_type="assistant",
484 )
485 probe.tick()
486 payload = hb.snapshot()
487 assert payload["sign_of_life_signal"] == "tool_child"
488 assert "uv run pytest" in payload["sign_of_life_evidence"]
489 preserved_timestamp = payload["last_sign_of_life_at"]
490
491 # Tick 3: the tool child is gone and CPU is flat (same reading as tick 2)
492 # -> null, and the previous last_sign_of_life_at is left untouched.
493 (proc_root / "2").rename(proc_root / "2-gone")
494 probe.tick()
495 payload = hb.snapshot()
496 assert payload["sign_of_life_signal"] is None
497 assert payload["last_sign_of_life_at"] == preserved_timestamp

237def _write_proc_stat(
238 proc_root: Path,
239 pid: int,
240 *,
241 ppid: int,
242 state: str = "R",
243 comm: str = "proc",
244 utime: int = 0,
245 stime: int = 0,
246) -> None:
247 """A fake ``/proc/<pid>/stat`` line, with a parenthesised ``comm`` that may
248 itself contain a space — the case that makes naive whitespace-splitting of
249 the whole line wrong and forces splitting after the last ``)`` instead."""
250 d = proc_root / str(pid)
251 d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
252 rest = [
253 state,
254 str(ppid),
255 "1",
256 "1",
257 "0",
258 "-1",
259 "0",
260 "0",
261 "0",
262 "0",
263 "0",
264 str(utime),
265 str(stime),
266 "0",
267 "0",
268 "20",
269 "0",
270 "1",
271 "0",
272 "1000",
273 ]
274 (d / "stat").write_text(f"{pid} ({comm}) " + " ".join(rest) + "\n")

436def test_transitions_log_exactly_once_entering_and_exactly_once_leaving_not_live(tmp_path):
437 """40 ticks, 15s apart, window 60s: the child goes silent at tick 5 and an
438 event returns at tick 30. Exactly one `not live for` line and exactly one
439 `live again` line, nothing in between."""
440 paths = RunPaths(tmp_path, "r1")
441 hb = RoundHeartbeat(paths, "g1")
442 config = LivenessConfig(window_seconds=60)
443 logs: list[str] = []
444 state = {"i": 0}
445
446 def clock() -> float:
447 return state["i"] * 15.0
448
449 def activity_provider() -> ChildActivity:
450 i = state["i"]
451 # Silent from tick 5 onward (frozen at tick 4's timestamp) until an
452 # event returns at tick 30.
453 event_tick = i if (i < 5 or i >= 30) else 4
454 at = datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(event_tick * 15.0, tz=datetime.UTC).isoformat(
455 timespec="milliseconds"
456 )
457 return _child(pid=1, spawned_at=at, last_event_at=at, last_event_type="assistant")
458
459 probe = LivenessProbe(
460 hb, config, activity_provider, log=logs.append, proc_root=tmp_path / "proc", clock=clock
461 )
462
463 for i in range(40):
464 state["i"] = i
465 probe.tick()
466
467 not_live_lines = [line for line in logs if "not live for" in line]
468 live_again_lines = [line for line in logs if "live again" in line]
469 assert len(not_live_lines) == 1
470 assert len(live_again_lines) == 1
471 assert not_live_lines[0] == (
472 "group g1 generation 0: not live for 1m15s in unknown phase — no signal"
473 )
474 assert live_again_lines[0].startswith("group g1 generation 0: live again: event ")

g7: suspend-detect — a machine suspend is a recorded fact on the run-scoped heartbeat, sampled by the driver lock's thread

u4: [liveness] `SuspendMonitor` samples `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` vs `CLOCK_BOOTTIME` on every driver-record tick (fallback: a wall-clock gap larger than five intervals), logs `machine suspend detected: <gap>` once per suspend, and stamps `last_wake_at` / `last_suspend_gap_s` / `suspends` on `<run>/heartbeat.json`; `DriverLock` starts and stops it, and `read_suspend_facts(paths)` gives group probes the wake time.

Plan section U4

U4. suspend-detect — a machine suspend is a recorded fact on the run-scoped heartbeat, sampled by the driver lock's thread

  • Summary: [liveness] SuspendMonitor samples CLOCK_MONOTONIC vs CLOCK_BOOTTIME on every driver-record tick (fallback: a wall-clock gap larger than five intervals), logs machine suspend detected: <gap> once per suspend, and stamps last_wake_at / last_suspend_gap_s / suspends on <run>/heartbeat.json; DriverLock starts and stops it, and read_suspend_facts(paths) gives group probes the wake time.
  • Goal: liveness.py SuspendMonitor(paths, *, gap_s, interval_s, log, clock=time.monotonic, boottime=lambda: time.clock_gettime(time.CLOCK_BOOTTIME), wall=time.time) with a pure sample() method returning a detected gap or None: boot-time delta minus monotonic delta > gap_s → suspend of that gap; else wall delta > 5 × interval_s → suspend of the wall delta. On detection it merges {"schema_version", "last_wake_at" (wall ISO), "last_suspend_gap_s", "suspends" (count), "updated_at"} into the run-scoped heartbeat file via atomic_write_text (keeping any keys already there) and logs one run-log line. DriverLock.acquire() constructs it with gap_s = config.liveness.suspend_gap_seconds (passed in by the caller in cli.py through a new DriverLock(paths, *, suspend_gap_s=…) kwarg with default 60 so existing callers and tests need no change) and calls sample() from the existing record thread; release() stops it. read_suspend_facts(paths) -> SuspendFacts | None reads the file tolerantly. Every write is best-effort like the heartbeat.

528#: Schema for the suspend facts merged into the run-scoped heartbeat file.
529#: Independent of ``heartbeat.SCHEMA_VERSION`` — this module never imports
530#: ``heartbeat.py`` (that module imports this one, for ``ChildActivity``), so
531#: bumping one on its own never forces a bump of the other.
532SUSPEND_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1
533
534
535def _run_heartbeat_path(paths: RunPaths) -> Path:
536 """Same file ``heartbeat.heartbeat_path(paths, group_id=None)`` names,
537 duplicated rather than imported: ``heartbeat.py`` already imports
538 ``ChildActivity`` from this module, and importing back would make the two
539 circular. Post-ADR-0007 runs never write a run-scoped heartbeat for phase
540 facts, which is exactly what leaves this file free for suspend facts."""
541 return paths.run_dir / "heartbeat.json"
542
543
544@dataclass
545class SuspendFacts:
546 """What ``<run>/heartbeat.json`` says about machine suspends so far."""
547
548 last_wake_at: str | None
549 last_suspend_gap_s: float | None
550 suspends: int
551
552
553def read_suspend_facts(paths: RunPaths) -> SuspendFacts | None:
554 """The suspend facts on disk, or ``None`` when none have ever been
555 written — tolerant of a missing, malformed, or pre-suspend-facts file,
556 same contract as ``heartbeat.read_heartbeat``."""
557 try:
558 payload = json.loads(_run_heartbeat_path(paths).read_text())
559 except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
560 return None
561 if not isinstance(payload, dict) or "last_wake_at" not in payload:
562 return None
563 return SuspendFacts(
564 last_wake_at=payload.get("last_wake_at"),
565 last_suspend_gap_s=payload.get("last_suspend_gap_s"),
566 suspends=payload.get("suspends", 0),
567 )

569
570class SuspendMonitor:
571 """Detects a machine suspend by comparing ``CLOCK_MONOTONIC`` (frozen
572 while suspended) against ``CLOCK_BOOTTIME`` (keeps advancing) between two
573 samples, with a wall-clock fallback for a platform where the two clocks
574 do not diverge across a suspend (WSL2).
575
576 ``sample()`` is pure and side-effect-free except for the detection path:
577 it always advances the monitor's own baseline, and only when it detects a
578 gap does it write the run-scoped heartbeat file and log a line. The first
579 call after construction only establishes the baseline — there is nothing
580 to compare against yet — so it never reports a suspend.
581 """
582
583 def __init__(
584 self,
585 paths: RunPaths,
586 *,
587 gap_s: float,
588 interval_s: float,
589 log: Callable[[str], None],
590 clock: Callable[[], float] = time.monotonic,
591 boottime: Callable[[], float] = lambda: time.clock_gettime(time.CLOCK_BOOTTIME),
592 wall: Callable[[], float] = time.time,
593 ) -> None:
594 self.paths = paths
595 self.gap_s = gap_s
596 self.interval_s = interval_s
597 self._log = log
598 self._clock = clock
599 self._boottime = boottime
600 self._wall = wall
601 self._prev_mono: float | None = None
602 self._prev_boot: float | None = None
603 self._prev_wall: float | None = None
604
605 def sample(self) -> float | None:
606 mono = self._clock()
607 boot = self._boottime()
608 wall = self._wall()
609 gap: float | None = None
610 if self._prev_mono is not None:
611 mono_delta = mono - self._prev_mono
612 boot_delta = boot - self._prev_boot
613 wall_delta = wall - self._prev_wall
614 boot_gap = boot_delta - mono_delta
615 if boot_gap > self.gap_s:
616 gap = boot_gap
617 elif wall_delta > 5 * self.interval_s:
618 gap = wall_delta
619 self._prev_mono = mono
620 self._prev_boot = boot
621 self._prev_wall = wall
622 if gap is not None:
623 self._record(gap, wall)
624 return gap
625
626 def _record(self, gap: float, wall_now: float) -> None:
627 """Best-effort, like the heartbeat: an unwritable run directory loses
628 the evidence, never the run."""
629 try:
630 path = _run_heartbeat_path(self.paths)
631 try:
632 existing = json.loads(path.read_text())
633 if not isinstance(existing, dict):
634 existing = {}
635 except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
636 existing = {}
637 now_iso = datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(wall_now, tz=datetime.UTC).isoformat(
638 timespec="seconds"
639 )
640 existing.update(
641 {
642 "schema_version": SUSPEND_SCHEMA_VERSION,
643 "last_wake_at": now_iso,
644 "last_suspend_gap_s": gap,
645 "suspends": existing.get("suspends", 0) + 1,
646 "updated_at": now_iso,
647 }
648 )
649 atomic_write_text(path, json.dumps(existing, indent=2) + "\n")
650 except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 - evidence is never worth the run
651 pass
652 self._log_line(f"machine suspend detected: {_humanize_age(gap)}")
653
654 def _log_line(self, line: str) -> None:
655 try:
656 self._log(line)
657 except Exception: # noqa: BLE001 - evidence is never worth the run
658 pass

g8: suspend-cure — after a detected suspend, a child with no Sign of Life since the wake is killed by pid tree and warm-resumed in place, counted and capped per generation

u5: [liveness] The probe cures (SIGTERM the child + `/proc` descendants, `kill_grace_seconds`, SIGKILL, mark cured) only when `last_wake_at` is set and the child has had no Sign of Life since it for a whole window and `cures < max_cures_per_generation`; the review loop routes every worker call through `_worker_call`, which catches `SuspendCured` and warm-resumes the same session id in the same generation; `GroupRunState.cures` (per generation) is persisted through a new `GroupContext.record_cure`, never touching `reentry_count`.

Plan section U5

U5. suspend-cure — after a detected suspend, a child with no Sign of Life since the wake is killed by pid tree and warm-resumed in place, counted and capped per generation

  • Summary: [liveness] The probe cures (SIGTERM the child + /proc descendants, kill_grace_seconds, SIGKILL, mark cured) only when last_wake_at is set and the child has had no Sign of Life since it for a whole window and cures < max_cures_per_generation; the review loop routes every worker call through _worker_call, which catches SuspendCured and warm-resumes the same session id in the same generation; GroupRunState.cures (per generation) is persisted through a new GroupContext.record_cure, never touching reentry_count.
  • Goal: liveness.py kill_tree(pid, *, grace_s, proc_root, kill=os.kill): SIGTERM to pid and descendants(pid), wait up to grace_s for each to disappear, SIGKILL the rest; returns the pids signalled. LivenessProbe gets suspend_facts_provider (reads read_suspend_facts(paths)), cures_provider() -> int and on_cure(pid, generation, session_id); the cure condition is last_wake_at is not None and max(last_sign_of_life_at, child_spawned_at) < last_wake_at and now − last_wake_at > liveness_window_s and cures < max; on cure it logs group <gid> generation <n>: suspend cure <k>/<max> — no sign of life since wake at <t>; killing session <sid> pid <pid>, calls activity.mark_cured(pid), kill_tree, and on_cure. Past the cap it logs once … cures exhausted (<max>/<max>); reporting only and never kills again in that generation. scheduler.py: GroupRunState.cures: dict[str, int] keyed by generation as a string (JSON-safe), GroupContext.record_cure: Callable[[], int] increments the current generation's count, persists state.json, returns the new count; reentry_count is untouched by a cure. review.py: _worker_call(fn, *, session_id, role, **kwargs) wraps every asyncio.to_thread(runner.…) site (first launch, revision resume, reviewer launch, re-review, extra pass, answer resume, re-entry resume, and the nudge_until_report call); on SuspendCured it logs group <gid> generation <n>: warm-resuming session <sid> after suspend cure and re-issues runner.resume(session_id, prompt=render_reentry_prompt(group) | render_re_review_prompt(report_path), cwd, on_turn) through the same wrapper (so a second cure re-issues again until the cap); the round then continues with the resumed result. The heartbeat's probe is given the loop's cures_provider (entry.cures.get(str(generation), 0)) and on_cure (→ ctx.record_cure()). A SuspendCured raised from a first-launch start_worker whose session never registered (no transcript yet) falls through to the existing SessionError path (documented in the wrapper's docstring). The _reenter fallback except SessionError is placed after the wrapper so a cure never forks a fresh generation.

274def kill_tree(
275 pid: int,
276 *,
277 grace_s: float,
278 proc_root: Path = Path("/proc"),
279 kill: Callable[[int, int], None] = os.kill,
280 sleep: Callable[[float], None] = time.sleep,
281 clock: Callable[[], float] = time.time,
282) -> list[int]:
283 """The Suspend Cure's kill (plan U5): SIGTERM *pid* and every live
284 descendant found under *proc_root*, wait up to *grace_s* for each to
285 disappear, then SIGKILL whatever is left. Returns every pid the SIGTERM
286 reached (not just the ones that needed the SIGKILL follow-up) — the
287 caller's evidence of what it actually signalled.
288
289 A pid that has already exited before its SIGTERM — the child died on its
290 own between the probe's read and this call, or a descendant snapshot that
291 raced an exit — is skipped without raising, same contract every ``/proc``
292 reader in this module holds. Descendants are read once, up front: a
293 process tree that changes shape mid-kill is not re-walked, since the goal
294 is "the tree this probe observed," not a moving target.
295 """
296 targets = [pid, *(child.pid for child in descendants(pid, proc_root=proc_root))]
297 signalled: list[int] = []
298 for target in targets:
299 try:
300 kill(target, signal.SIGTERM)
301 except ProcessLookupError:
302 continue
303 signalled.append(target)
304
305 deadline = clock() + grace_s
306 remaining = set(signalled)
307 while remaining and clock() < deadline:
308 remaining = {t for t in remaining if _proc_alive(t, proc_root)}
309 if remaining:
310 sleep(0.05)
311 for target in remaining:
312 if _proc_alive(target, proc_root):
313 try:
314 kill(target, signal.SIGKILL)
315 except ProcessLookupError:
316 pass
317 return signalled
318

393def should_cure(
394 *,
395 last_wake_at: str | None,
396 last_sign_of_life_at: str | None,
397 child_spawned_at: str,
398 now: float,
399 window_s: float,
400) -> bool:
401 """The Suspend Cure eligibility predicate (plan U5) — everything except
402 the per-generation cap, which the caller checks separately so it can
403 still log "cures exhausted" for a child that is otherwise eligible.
404
405 Pure and side-effect-free so the table of cases tests directly: no cure
406 without a recorded machine wake (R7's last sentence — Not Live alone is
407 never enough, no matter how long); no cure when a Sign of Life has been
408 seen since that wake; no cure until a whole Liveness Window has passed
409 since the wake.
410 """
411 if last_wake_at is None:
412 return False
413 wake = _parse_ts(last_wake_at)
414 if wake is None:
415 return False
416 candidates = [_parse_ts(last_sign_of_life_at), _parse_ts(child_spawned_at)]
417 baselines = [b for b in candidates if b is not None]
418 baseline = max(baselines) if baselines else None
419 if baseline is not None and baseline >= wake:
420 return False
421 return now - wake > window_s

432 async def _worker_call(self, thunk: Callable[[], object], *, recover: Callable[[str], object]):
433 """Runs one worker call in a thread; on a Suspend Cure (plan U5) — the
434 liveness probe having killed this child because it showed no Sign of
435 Life since a detected machine wake — logs the recovery and re-issues
436 ``recover(cured_session_id)`` in *this call's* place, itself routed
437 back through ``_worker_call`` so a second cure re-issues again until
438 the probe's own per-generation cap stops curing. Coder call sites pass
439 a ``recover`` that warm-resumes with the re-entry prompt; reviewer
440 sites pass one that resumes with the re-review prompt (per the U5
441 decision) — the wrapper itself is role-agnostic.
442
443 Any other exception — a plain ``SessionError``, ``UsageLimit``, a
444 future ``ContentFiltered`` — propagates unchanged; this wrapper is
445 transparent to everything but ``SuspendCured``. A ``SuspendCured``
446 from a first launch whose session never registered on disk still
447 carries a real ``session_id`` (read off the argv the failed call
448 actually used, not off the transcript), so ``recover`` resumes it the
449 same as any other cure; being a ``SessionError`` subclass, it would
450 fall through to the ordinary failure handling regardless if it ever
451 turned up somewhere this wrapper does not reach.
452 """
453 try:
454 return await asyncio.to_thread(thunk)
455 except SuspendCured as exc:
456 self._log(
457 f"group {self.gid} generation {self.generation}: "
458 f"warm-resuming session {exc.session_id} after suspend cure"
459 )
460 return await self._worker_call(partial(recover, exc.session_id), recover=recover)
461

680def test_cure_predicate_no_wake_recorded_is_never_a_cure_even_after_two_windows():
681 """R7's last sentence: Not Live alone, with no machine wake behind it, is
682 never a cure — no matter how long the silence has run."""
683 now = 10_000.0
684 window = 60.0

686 should_cure(
687 last_wake_at=None,
688 last_sign_of_life_at=_iso(now - 3 * window),
689 child_spawned_at=_iso(now - 3 * window),
690 now=now,
691 window_s=window,
692 )
693 is False
694 )

702 should_cure(

729def test_cure_predicate_at_the_cap_kills_nothing_and_logs_exactly_one_exhausted_line(tmp_path):
730 paths = RunPaths(tmp_path, "r1")
731 hb = RoundHeartbeat(paths, "g1")
732 config = LivenessConfig(window_seconds=60, max_cures_per_generation=1)
733 now = 10_000.0
734 wake = now - 61 # past the window since the wake — otherwise eligible
735
736 def clock() -> float:
737 return now
738
739 def activity_provider() -> ChildActivity:
740 return _child(
741 pid=1,
742 spawned_at=_iso(wake - 200),
743 last_event_at=_iso(wake - 100), # too old to count as Sign of Life
744 last_event_type="assistant",
745 )
746
747 logs: list[str] = []
748 killed: list[int] = []
749
750 probe = LivenessProbe(
751 hb,
752 config,
753 activity_provider,
754 log=logs.append,
755 proc_root=tmp_path / "proc",
756 clock=clock,
757 suspend_facts_provider=lambda: SuspendFacts(
758 last_wake_at=_iso(wake), last_suspend_gap_s=100.0, suspends=1
759 ),
760 cures_provider=lambda: 1, # already at the cap (max_cures_per_generation=1)
761 kill=lambda pid, sig: killed.append(pid),
762 )
763
764 probe.tick()
765
766 assert killed == []
767 exhausted = [line for line in logs if "cures exhausted" in line]
768 assert len(exhausted) == 1
769 assert "1/1" in exhausted[0]
770
771 # A second tick must not repeat the line — logged exactly once.
772 probe.tick()
773 exhausted = [line for line in logs if "cures exhausted" in line]
774 assert len(exhausted) == 1

866def test_cure_returns_kill_tree_of_a_real_worker_child_makes_wait_nonzero_and_registry_cured(
867 fake_home, tmp_path
868):
869 """The `_is_same_process`/`kill_tree` interplay g8-6 asks for: a real
870 `claude`-shaped child (`fake_claude.py` spawned through `StreamingProcess`,
871 exactly the way `SessionRunner._spawn` does it) is killed by `kill_tree`,
872 and both halves of what the review loop relies on hold — the stream
873 reports a nonzero exit promptly, and the activity registry (marked cured
874 the same way the probe would) still answers for the dead pid."""
875 script(fake_home, {"result": "OK", "delay_s": 30})
876 argv = [*STREAM_ARGV, "--session-id", "66666666-6666-6666-6666-666666666666"]
877 env = {**os.environ, "FAKE_CLAUDE_HOME": str(fake_home)}
878 grace_s = 2.0
879
880 registry = ActivityRegistry()
881 stream = StreamingProcess(argv, cwd=tmp_path, env=env)
882 stream.start(prompt="go")
883 registry.spawned(stream.pid, session_id="s1", cwd=str(tmp_path))
884 time.sleep(0.3) # let the child actually start sleeping on its delay
885
886 start = time.monotonic()
887 kill_tree(stream.pid, grace_s=grace_s)
888 registry.mark_cured(stream.pid)
889 outcome = stream.wait()
890 elapsed = time.monotonic() - start
891
892 assert outcome.returncode != 0
893 assert elapsed < grace_s + 2.0
894 assert registry.was_cured(stream.pid) is True

1"""U5 tests: a `SuspendCured` raised at a worker call site is warm-resumed in
2place — coder and reviewer alike — counted and capped per generation (plan
3U5). Sessions are scripted in-process via `StubRunner` (see `test_review_loop`),
4zero subprocesses, zero tokens.
5"""
6

14from orchestrator.execution.review import make_executor
15from orchestrator.execution.scheduler import GroupContext, GroupState, Scheduler

21class CuringStubRunner(StubRunner):
22 """A `StubRunner` whose *Nth* `resume()` call (1-indexed, across every
23 session) raises `SuspendCured` instead of returning — modelling a
24 liveness probe having just killed that child — then behaves exactly like
25 `StubRunner` on every other call, including the very next one (the
26 review loop's own warm-resume recovery).
27 """
28
29 def __init__(self, fork_scripts, *, cure_on_resume_call: int, on_cure=None):
30 super().__init__(fork_scripts)
31 self._cure_on_resume_call = cure_on_resume_call
32 self._on_cure = on_cure
33 self._resume_calls = 0
34 self.cured_session_id: str | None = None
35
36 def resume(self, *, session_id, prompt, cwd, json_schema=None, on_turn=None):
37 self._resume_calls += 1
38 if self._resume_calls == self._cure_on_resume_call:
39 self.cured_session_id = session_id
40 if self._on_cure is not None:
41 self._on_cure()
42 raise SuspendCured(
43 f"claude exited 137 (--resume {session_id}): killed as a suspend cure",
44 session_id,
45 )
46 return super().resume(
47 session_id=session_id, prompt=prompt, cwd=cwd, json_schema=json_schema, on_turn=on_turn
48 )
49
50
51def _scheduled_context(harness: Harness, group, scheduler: Scheduler) -> GroupContext:
52 """A real `GroupContext` wired to a real `Scheduler` (for `record_cure`'s
53 persistence to `state.json`) but driving the group directly through
54 `make_executor`, bypassing the scheduler's own admission loop — the same
55 thing `Scheduler._run_group` does, minus the DAG bookkeeping this test
56 does not exercise."""
57 return GroupContext(
58 group=group,
59 generation=1,
60 set_state=lambda state: scheduler.set_state(group.id, state),
61 set_generation=lambda generation: scheduler.set_generation(group.id, generation),
62 record_cure=lambda: scheduler.record_cure(group.id),
63 )
64
65
66async def _never_called_executor(ctx) -> GroupState: # pragma: no cover
67 raise AssertionError("scheduler.run() was never invoked by this test")
68

g2: content-filter-kind — a content-filter error is its own failure kind, never warm-resumed, routed like a blocked coder with the last assistant message quoted

u10: [failure-routes] `ContentFiltered(SessionError)` is raised by `_invoke` when the error text matches the content-filter phrase, carrying `last_assistant_text`; the review loop's `_worker_call` catches it before any generic `SessionError` handler and escalates `CODER_BLOCKED` quoting that text, then `retry` → relaunch, `answer` → rewrite, no answer → rewrite with a context surprise naming the filter.

146class ContentFiltered(SessionError):
147 """The API's content filter blocked the round's output (plan U10).
148
149 A distinct type because the right response is neither "retry the same
150 session" (``_reenter``'s fallback) nor "fork a fresh generation and hope"
151 (a plain ``SessionError``): the review loop escalates this as a blocked
152 coder quoting the last thing the model actually said, then either
153 relaunches on the same spec (operator fixed something upstream) or
154 rewrites with the filter named as a surprise. Never warm-resumed — the
155 session that produced the blocked output is not one to resume as-is.
156
157 ``last_assistant_text`` is ``StreamOutcome.last_assistant_text`` (plan
158 U1) — the child may never have produced an envelope at all (a filtered
159 nonzero exit) or produced one whose own ``result`` *is* the filter
160 notice, so the stream's own record of the last real turn is the only
161 place the pre-filter text can come from.
162 """
163
164 def __init__(self, message: str, last_assistant_text: str = ""):
165 super().__init__(message)
166 self.last_assistant_text = last_assistant_text
167
168
169#: How the API's content filter announces itself on the wire — evidence, not
170#: guesswork, per the wording actually seen (learning_podcast run
171#: r20260907-123644 g1): ``API Error: Output blocked by content filtering
172#: policy``. Matched against the same failure text ``is_usage_limit`` reads,
173#: on both the nonzero-exit and the ``is_error`` envelope paths.
174_CONTENT_FILTER_RE = re.compile(
175 r"content filter(?:ing)? policy|blocked by content filter",
176 re.IGNORECASE,
177)
178
179
180def is_content_filtered(detail: str) -> bool:
181 """Whether a failure detail is the API's content filter rather than an
182 ordinary broken call or a usage limit."""
183 return bool(_CONTENT_FILTER_RE.search(detail))

2
3``-k classify``/``-k phrase`` exercise ``SessionRunner._invoke`` against
4``tests/fake_claude.py`` (zero live CLI calls, zero tokens, plan R24) —
5matching ``tests/test_sessions.py``'s convention. ``-k hitl``/``-k
6autonomous`` exercise the review loop's routing in-process against
7``StubRunner`` (see ``tests/test_review_loop.py``) — matching
8``tests/test_suspend_cure.py``'s convention for a `_worker_call`-routed
9exception.
10"""

136class ContentFilteringStubRunner(StubRunner):
137 """A ``StubRunner`` whose *Nth* launch or resume call raises
138 ``ContentFiltered`` instead of returning — modelling the API's content
139 filter having blocked that round — then behaves exactly like
140 ``StubRunner`` on every other call. Mirrors
141 ``test_suspend_cure.CuringStubRunner``'s shape for the same reason: this
142 is a `_worker_call`-routed exception too, just one that must never be
143 warm-resumed.
144 """
145
146 def __init__(
147 self,
148 fork_scripts,
149 *,
150 filter_on_launch_call: int | None = None,
151 filter_on_resume_call: int | None = None,
152 last_assistant_text: str = "here is what I was drafting",
153 ):
154 super().__init__(fork_scripts)
155 self._filter_on_launch_call = filter_on_launch_call
156 self._filter_on_resume_call = filter_on_resume_call
157 self._last_assistant_text = last_assistant_text
158 self._launch_calls = 0
159 self._resume_calls = 0
160
161 def _launch(self, prompt, name, session_id, on_turn):
162 self._launch_calls += 1
163 if self._launch_calls == self._filter_on_launch_call:
164 raise ContentFiltered(
165 "claude reported an error result: API Error: Output blocked by "
166 "content filtering policy",
167 self._last_assistant_text,
168 )
169 return super()._launch(prompt, name, session_id, on_turn)
170
171 def resume(self, *, session_id, prompt, cwd, json_schema=None, on_turn=None):
172 self._resume_calls += 1
173 if self._resume_calls == self._filter_on_resume_call:
174 raise ContentFiltered(
175 "claude reported an error result: API Error: Output blocked by "
176 "content filtering policy",
177 self._last_assistant_text,
178 )
179 return super().resume(
180 session_id=session_id, prompt=prompt, cwd=cwd, json_schema=json_schema, on_turn=on_turn
181 )
182
183
184def on_stuck(source: str = "workers_via_orchestrator") -> EscalationPolicy:
185 return EscalationPolicy("on_stuck", source)
186

g9: activity-tail — the last five worker actions read from a session transcript, as a helper for `status` and the Observatory

u6: [visibility] `transcript_events.activity_tail(path, *, n=5) -> list[ActivityEntry]` returns the last `n` tool calls of a Claude Code transcript (time, tool name, first line of the tool input, returned yes/no) without persisting anything; `format_activity_tail(entries)` renders the `status` lines.

Plan section U6

U6. activity-tail — the last five worker actions read from a session transcript, as a helper for status and the Observatory

  • Summary: [visibility] transcript_events.activity_tail(path, *, n=5) -> list[ActivityEntry] returns the last n tool calls of a Claude Code transcript (time, tool name, first line of the tool input, returned yes/no) without persisting anything; format_activity_tail(entries) renders the status lines.
  • Goal: ActivityEntry pydantic model (at: str | None, tool: str, input_head: str — first line of the JSON-ish input, capped at 120 chars, returned: bool) built from parse_transcript events: each tool_use event is an entry; returned is true iff a later role == "tool" event carries the same tool_use_id. 85/** Same rendering as `heartbeat._humanize` / `liveness._humanize_age`. */
86function humanizeAge(seconds: number): string {
87 const total = Math.max(0, Math.floor(seconds));
88 const hours = Math.floor(total / 3600);
89 const minutes = Math.floor((total % 3600) / 60);
90 const secs = total % 60;
91 if (hours) return `${hours}h${String(minutes).padStart(2, "0")}m`;
92 if (minutes) return `${minutes}m${String(secs).padStart(2, "0")}s`;
93 return `${secs}s`;
94}
95
96/**
97 * Seconds past the Liveness Window since the child last showed a Sign of
98 * Life, or `null` when it is live, there is no child, or the heartbeat
99 * predates these facts — the client-side twin of `liveness.not_live_age`.
100 */
101function notLiveAgeS(heartbeat: NonNullable<SnapshotGroup["heartbeat"]>, nowS: number): number | null {
102 if (heartbeat.child_pid == null) return null;
103 const window = heartbeat.liveness_window_s;
104 if (window == null) return null;
105 const baselines = [
106 timeMs(heartbeat.last_sign_of_life_at) ?? undefined,
107 timeMs(heartbeat.child_spawned_at) ?? undefined,
108 ].filter((value): value is number => value !== undefined);
109 if (baselines.length === 0) return null;
110 const age = nowS - Math.max(...baselines) / 1000;
111 return age > window ? age : null;
112}
113
114/**
115 * One human-readable line for the board, derived entirely from the
116 * heartbeat's own facts — the same four shapes and the same derivation rule
117 * `orchestrator/execution/liveness.py`'s `liveness_line` applies for `status`,
118 * so the two surfaces can never disagree. Never a state the backend sent.
119 */
120function livenessLine(group: SnapshotGroup): { text: string; notLive: boolean } | null {
121 const heartbeat = group.heartbeat;
122 if (!heartbeat || heartbeat.liveness_window_s == null) return null;
123 const phase = heartbeat.phase || "unknown phase";
124 if (heartbeat.child_pid == null) return { text: `no worker child (${phase})`, notLive: false };
125 const nowS = Date.now() / 1000;
126 const age = notLiveAgeS(heartbeat, nowS);
127 if (age !== null) {
128 const evidence = heartbeat.sign_of_life_evidence || "no evidence recorded";
129 return { text: `NOT LIVE for ${humanizeAge(age)} in ${phase} — ${evidence}`, notLive: true };
130 }
131 const lastMs = timeMs(heartbeat.last_sign_of_life_at);
132 const liveAge = lastMs != null ? nowS - lastMs / 1000 : 0;
133 return { text: `live: ${heartbeat.sign_of_life_signal} ${humanizeAge(liveAge)} ago`, notLive: false };
134}
135
136/** The group's newest session by generation, then by whichever wrote most
137 * recently within that generation — what "the group's newest session" means
138 * for the activity tail. */
139function newestSession(group: SnapshotGroup): SnapshotSession | null {
140 let newest: SnapshotSession | null = null;
141 for (const session of group.sessions) {
142 if (!newest) {
143 newest = session;
144 continue;
145 }
146 if (session.generation !== newest.generation) {
147 if (session.generation > newest.generation) newest = session;
148 continue;
149 }
150 const a = timeMs(session.transcript_mtime) ?? timeMs(session.started_at) ?? 0;
151 const b = timeMs(newest.transcript_mtime) ?? timeMs(newest.started_at) ?? 0;
152 if (a >= b) newest = session;
153 }
154 return newest;
155}
156
157function activityTailOf(group: SnapshotGroup): ActivityEntry[] {
158 return newestSession(group)?.activity_tail ?? [];
159}

Upstream groups:

  • g11 provides decision-ledger — u8-decision-ledger: [decisions] EscalationResponse.binding: bool = True, answer_escalation(..., binding=True), the Observatory POST body's binding field, and new orchestrator/execution/decisions.py computing decision_ledger(paths, group_id) from both escalation locations (answered coder_question requests with action answer and binding true, ordered by time) and rendering ## Operator decisions (binding) verbatim; the bundle export passes the flag through.
  • g6 provides liveness-line — u3-not-live-report: [liveness] The probe writes one run-log Lifecycle Event on entering Not Live (group <gid> generation <n>: not live for <age> in <phase> — <evidence>) and one on leaving (… live again: <signal> <age> ago), never per tick; driver_status_line stops saying progressing from the heartbeat mtime and reports how many active groups are live and how many are not; liveness.py ships liveness_line(heartbeat: dict, *, now) -> str and cures_exhausted_line(heartbeat, run_id, driver_pid) -> str | None for status (wired in U12) and the same derivation rule the Observatory applies.
  • g8 provides u5-suspend-cure — u5-suspend-cure: [liveness] The probe cures (SIGTERM the child + /proc descendants, kill_grace_seconds, SIGKILL, mark cured) only when last_wake_at is set and the child has had no Sign of Life since it for a whole window and cures < max_cures_per_generation; the review loop routes every worker call through _worker_call, which catches SuspendCured and warm-resumes the same session id in the same generation; GroupRunState.cures (per generation) is persisted through a new GroupContext.record_cure, never touching reentry_count.
  • g9 provides activity-tail — u6-activity-tail: [visibility] transcript_events.activity_tail(path, *, n=5) -> list[ActivityEntry] returns the last n tool calls of a Claude Code transcript (time, tool name, first line of the tool input, returned yes/no) without persisting anything; format_activity_tail(entries) renders the status lines.

  • g5 consumes u13-skill-cadence — u13-skill-cadence: [docs] SKILL.md Phase 2 drops the manual wedge check and the 20–30 minute heartbeat; Monitor conditions add the not live for, live again, machine suspend detected, suspend cure and cures exhausted lines and the fallback status runs at most hourly; the manual kill -INT -<pgid> + resume is reserved for a group status reports Not Live with cures exhausted or no suspend detected; triage-guide.md's coder_question section says answer binds by default, --guidance opts out, and drops the "lives only in that coder's session" paragraph.

221def start_time(pid: int, *, proc_root: Path = Path("/proc")) -> float | None:
222 """Wall-clock epoch seconds the process started (``stat`` field 22 over
223 the ``btime`` line of ``<proc_root>/stat``), or ``None`` when either read
224 fails — a raced exit, or a fake tree with no ``btime``."""
225 fields = _read_stat_fields(pid, proc_root)
226 if fields is None or len(fields) < 20:
227 return None
228 try:
229 ticks = int(fields[19])
230 btime = next(
231 int(line.split()[1])
232 for line in (proc_root / "stat").read_text().splitlines()
233 if line.startswith("btime ")
234 )
235 except (OSError, ValueError, IndexError, StopIteration):
236 return None
237 return btime + ticks / os.sysconf("SC_CLK_TCK")

165 assert exit_code == 0

tests/test_liveness_live.py
@@ -0,0 +1,219 @@
1"""Plan U14 — Not Live end to end against a real `claude` child.
2
3Everything below this tier (`tests/test_liveness.py`) proves the Sign of Life
4mechanism against a synthetic `activity_provider` and a fake `/proc` tree. This
5test is the one place a *real* worker child is frozen with `SIGSTOP` and the
6whole stack — the heartbeat tick, the run log, and `status` — is asked to
7notice, in that order, without any of it knowing the freeze was deliberate.
8
9**This tier spends real tokens** (one sonnet coder round). Excluded from a
10plain `pytest` by `addopts = -m "not llm"`; opt in with `uv run pytest -m llm`.
11"""
12
13from __future__ import annotations
14
15import json
16import os
17import shutil
18import signal
19import subprocess
20import sys
21import time
22from pathlib import Path
23
24import pytest
25
26from orchestrator.execution.manifest import RunPaths
27from orchestrator.grouping.pipeline import serialize_grouping
28from orchestrator.model import Group, GroupingResult, ReviewIntensity, VerificationItem
29
30pytestmark = [
31 pytest.mark.llm,
32 pytest.mark.skipif(shutil.which("claude") is None, reason="claude CLI not on PATH"),
33]
34
35#: `window_seconds = 20` in the fixture's own config; polled well past both the
36#: heartbeat's 15s tick and the window, short of "something is actually wrong".
37NOT_LIVE_POLL_DEADLINE_S = 60.0
38RUN_TIMEOUT_S = 900.0
39
40
41def _git(repo: Path, *args: str) -> str:
42 done = subprocess.run(["git", *args], cwd=repo, capture_output=True, text=True)
43 assert done.returncode == 0, f"git {' '.join(args)}: {done.stderr}"
44 return done.stdout
45
46
47def _orchestrate_bin() -> Path:
48 """This worktree's own console script — never the operator's globally
49 installed `smart-mcps-orchestrate`, which may be a different version."""
50 return Path(sys.executable).parent / "smart-mcps-orchestrate"
51
52
53@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
54def liveness_repo(tmp_path_factory) -> Path:
55 repo = tmp_path_factory.mktemp("liveness-repo")
56 _git(repo, "init", "-q", "-b", "main")
57 _git(repo, "config", "user.email", "live@test")
58 _git(repo, "config", "user.name", "live")
59 (repo / "README.md").write_text("# liveness live fixture\n")
60 (repo / "greeting.py").write_text('def greet():\n return "hello"\n')
61 (repo / "plan.md").write_text(
62 "# live plan\n\n## Tasks\n\n- T1: add a farewell() function beside greet()\n"
63 )
64 _git(repo, "add", "-A")
65 _git(repo, "commit", "-q", "-m", "init")
66
67 (repo / ".orchestrator").mkdir()
68 (repo / ".orchestrator" / "config.toml").write_text(
69 '[session]\nconfine = true\nmodel = "sonnet"\n\n'
70 "[escalation]\nenabled = false\n\n"
71 "[liveness]\nwindow_seconds = 20\n"
72 )
73
74 group = Group(
75 id="g1",
76 name="farewell",
77 summary="Add a farewell function.",
78 spec=(
79 "In greeting.py, add a function `farewell()` returning the string "
80 '"goodbye", right after `greet()`. Then commit the change. '
81 "Do not change anything else."
82 ),
83 difficulty=0.1,
84 intensity=ReviewIntensity.SELF_VERIFY,
85 files=["greeting.py"],
86 verification=[
87 VerificationItem(id="v1", description="farewell() exists and returns goodbye")
88 ],
89 )
90 grouping = repo / ".orchestrator" / "groupings" / "plan"
91 grouping.mkdir(parents=True)
92 (grouping / "groups.json").write_text(
93 serialize_grouping(GroupingResult(plan_path="plan.md", groups=[group]))
94 )
95 (grouping / "base-context.md").write_text(
96 "This is a tiny scratch repository used to verify Not Live end to end. "
97 "Keep every change minimal.\n"
98 )
99 return repo
100
101
102def _run_status(orchestrate: Path, repo: Path, run_id: str) -> str:
103 done = subprocess.run(
104 [str(orchestrate), "status", run_id, "--repo", str(repo)],
105 capture_output=True,
106 text=True,
107 )
108 return done.stdout
109
110
111def test_not_live_detected_and_cleared_on_a_real_sigstopped_child(liveness_repo: Path) -> None:
112 repo = liveness_repo
113 run_id = "liveness1"
114 orchestrate = _orchestrate_bin()
115 paths = RunPaths(repo, run_id)
116 log_path = repo / "run.log"
117
118 with log_path.open("w") as sink:
119 proc = subprocess.Popen(
120 [
121 str(orchestrate),
122 "run",
123 "--repo",
124 str(repo),
125 "--run-id",
126 run_id,
127 "--intensity",
128 "autonomous",
129 ],
130 stdout=sink,
131 stderr=sink,
132 )
133
134 child_pid: int | None = None
135 try:
136 # 1. Wait for a real worker child to be registered. Polls `proc.poll()`
137 # too: a run that fails before ever spawning a worker (a bad config, a
138 # denied write) should be reported immediately, not after the full
139 # timeout — the failure text is already sitting in `run.log`.
140 deadline = time.time() + RUN_TIMEOUT_S
141 while time.time() < deadline and child_pid is None:
142 if paths.state_path.is_file():
143 try:
144 state = json.loads(paths.state_path.read_text())
145 except json.JSONDecodeError:
146 state = {}
147 live_pids = state.get("live_pids") or {}
148 if live_pids:
149 child_pid = int(next(iter(live_pids)))
150 if child_pid is None:
151 if proc.poll() is not None:
152 break
153 time.sleep(1)
154 assert child_pid is not None, (
155 f"no worker child ever registered (run exited {proc.poll()})\n{log_path.read_text()}"
156 )
157
158 # 2. Freeze it. No suspend was ever recorded, so this must read as
159 # Not Live via the plain Sign of Life path, never a Suspend Cure.
160 os.kill(child_pid, signal.SIGSTOP)
161
162 # 3. Poll `status` until it reports Not Live with cpu-flat evidence.
163 not_live_deadline = time.time() + NOT_LIVE_POLL_DEADLINE_S
164 status_out = ""
165 while time.time() < not_live_deadline:
166 status_out = _run_status(orchestrate, repo, run_id)
167 if "liveness: NOT LIVE for" in status_out:
168 break
169 time.sleep(5)
170 assert "liveness: NOT LIVE for" in status_out, (
171 f"status never reported Not Live within {NOT_LIVE_POLL_DEADLINE_S:.0f}s\n{status_out}"
172 )
173 assert "cpu flat" in status_out, status_out
174 assert "suspend cure" not in log_path.read_text(), (
175 "no machine suspend was ever recorded — a cure firing here means the "
176 "cure predicate no longer requires a recorded wake"
177 )
178
179 # 4. `status` derives Not Live from the heartbeat's facts at read time;
180 # the probe logs the transition only on its own next tick (≤ 15 s
181 # later). Thawing before that tick would leave nothing to be "live
182 # again" from, so wait for the entering line first — it is asserted too.
183 entered_deadline = time.time() + NOT_LIVE_POLL_DEADLINE_S
184 while time.time() < entered_deadline:
185 if (
186 paths.event_log_path.is_file()
187 and "not live for" in paths.event_log_path.read_text()
188 ):
189 break
190 time.sleep(1)
191 assert paths.event_log_path.is_file() and (
192 "not live for" in paths.event_log_path.read_text()
193 ), f"the probe never logged entering Not Live\n{log_path.read_text()}"
194
195 # 5. Thaw it and confirm the run notices and finishes.
196 os.kill(child_pid, signal.SIGCONT)
197 live_again_deadline = time.time() + RUN_TIMEOUT_S
198 while time.time() < live_again_deadline:
199 if paths.event_log_path.is_file() and "live again" in paths.event_log_path.read_text():
200 break
201 time.sleep(2)
202 assert (
203 paths.event_log_path.is_file() and "live again" in paths.event_log_path.read_text()
204 ), f"no 'live again' line ever appeared\n{log_path.read_text()}"
205
206 exit_code = proc.wait(timeout=RUN_TIMEOUT_S)
207 output = log_path.read_text()
208 assert exit_code == 0, f"run exited {exit_code}\n{output}"
209 state = json.loads(paths.state_path.read_text())
210 assert state["groups"]["g1"]["state"] == "completed"
211 finally:
212 if proc.poll() is None:
213 if child_pid is not None:
214 try:
215 os.kill(child_pid, signal.SIGCONT)
216 except ProcessLookupError:
217 pass
218 proc.kill()
219 proc.wait(timeout=30)

1"""The liveness plumbing is wired into a real run, not only unit-tested.
2
3Plans U1/U2/U5 shipped `ActivityRegistry`, `LivenessProbe` and the Suspend Cure
4seams with green tests against directly-constructed objects, while nothing in
5`_cmd_run` ever built a registry or installed a probe — the same "mechanism
6tested, wiring absent" shape that once left Landlock dead for a release (see
7`test_confinement.py`). These tests assert the construction sites.
8"""
9

208## When status reports Not Live
209
210`status` derives its liveness line from the same facts as the `not live for`
211and `live again` lines in `logs/run.log` (plan U2/U3). Three cases:
212
213- **Live again on its own.** A `not live for …` line followed later by
214 `live again: …` with no action from you — the child was slow, not dead.
215 Nothing to do.
216- **Not live after a machine suspend, with Suspend Cures left.** A
217 `machine suspend detected: …` line precedes it and `status` (or
218 `cures exhausted`, see below) shows cures remaining this generation — the
219 probe will cure the child itself (kill and warm-resume in place). Wait for
220 the `suspend cure <k>/<max> — …` line rather than intervening.
221- **Not live with cures exhausted, or no suspend detected at all.** `status`
222 prints the `cures exhausted (<k>/<max> this generation) — kill -INT -<pgid> then smart-mcps-orchestrate resume <run_id>` line, or there was never a
223 `machine suspend detected` line to explain the silence. This is the one
224 case left that needs your hand: `kill -INT -<pgid>`, then `resume`.
225
